messages:
maya: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection change landed last night we're seeing a cluster of OOMs on p3x nodes when serving long contexts + heavy KV cache hits. Trace: https://go/trace/1963456789 . Looks like allocator pressure spikes during decode-stage coalescing.

tom: Can you paste the top-line numbers? latency vs memory?

jess: From a quick profile: sustained GPU mem climb ~200MB/sec during decode-prefill boundary. Worker logs show repeated allocate/evict churn. I dumped the per-slab stats:```
slab_sizes: [64K, 256K, 1M, 4M]
alloc_count: 120k
free_count: 118k
avg_live_frag: 23%
largest_free_fragment: 512K
` ```

ryan: Interesting — avg_live_frag is higher than baseline (was ~8% last week). Could be the new kernel's io pattern prevents buffer reuse. Any evidence of cross-request pinning?

jess: Yes — decode path holds transient KV segments until post-decode coalescer finishes; coalescer was changed to batch larger joins which extended lifetime. Perf traces: allocation peak aligns with coalescer windows.

maya: So hypothesis: kernel change enlarged coalescing windows -> longer buffer lifetimes -> fragmentation + spill -> eviction thrash. That + our per-request cap being too loose.

tom: Quick mitigation options? Reduce coalescer window, tighten per-request soft caps, or introduce small-buffer segregated pool to avoid large-slab fragmentation. Which is fastest?

jess: Fastest is feature-flagging the kernel selection fallback to previous kernel (roll back for canary) — low-risk and immediate. Medium: tighten per-request soft cap from 1.2x to 0.9x calibrated by bytes_of_kv. Longer: implement segregated small-buffer pool + coalesce-on-free to reduce fragmentation.

ryan: I prototyped a segregated pool in sandbox earlier — it reduced frag by ~12% on short sequences. Patch:```
// allocate from small pool when size <= 256K
if (size <= 256*1024) return small_pool.alloc(size);
else return big_pool.alloc(size);
```
Impact: lowered eviction count by ~18% in synthetic KV-heavy replay.

maya: Nice. For immediate action: 1) toggle kernel selection fallback for canary (deploy-bot can we push rollback flag to 10%?), 2) lower per-request soft-cap to 0.9x on canary, 3) run a perf replay with segregated-pool enabled on a staging subset. Can someone file a quick rollout plan?

deploy-bot: @maya rollout flag kernel_fallback=true set to 10% for cluster=p3x scheduled in 5m.

tom: I'll draft the rollout/rollback steps and perf validation criteria: - 1h smoke: no OOMs, 95p latency within +/-5% baseline - 4h: eviction rate down -24% or better - compare alloc churn graphs.

jess: Also capture KV cache occupancy curves and prefix-decode lifetime histograms. I suspect prefill vs decode-time sizing matters: we should test two eviction policies concurrently: A) prefill-first eviction (prioritize clearing prefill entries) B) decode-bound caps (evict earliest decode-held segments).

maya: Agree. Add perf-bot alert for memory slope > 50MB/min per worker so we catch regressions early.

perf-bot: Alert rule created: gpu_memory_slope > 50MB/min for 3m -> channel=eng-runtime.

ryan: I'll start sandbox run with segregated pool + coalesce-on-free and attach heap snapshots. Expect results in ~2h.

maya: Thanks. If sandbox numbers look good we'll promote canary to 50% and enable small-pool on canary nodes. Keep the thread updated with the two perf graphs (alloc rate, eviction rate). :thumbsup:
